# CMS Interoperability and Prior Authorization Final Rule (CMS-0057-F)

- Citation: CMS press release, 2024-01-17. https://www.cms.gov/newsroom/press-releases/cms-finalizes-rule-expand-access-health-information-improve-prior-authorization-process ; fact sheet: https://www.cms.gov/files/document/fact-sheet-cms-interoperability-and-prior-authorization-final-rule-cms-0057-f.pdf
- Year: 2024 (rule); provisions effective 2026 and 2027
- Tier: 1 (government)
- Method: federal regulation, not a study.
- Key provisions (quoted from the press release): from 2026, decisions within "72 hours for expedited (i.e., urgent) requests and seven calendar days for standard (i.e., non-urgent) requests"; payers must "include a specific reason for denying"; payers must "publicly report prior authorization metrics"; Prior Authorization API required "beginning January 2027". CMS estimates "approximately $15 billion of estimated savings over ten years".
- Limits: applies to MA, Medicaid/CHIP and federal-exchange QHPs; doesn't mention SNFs specifically. Seven days is long next to a hospital discharge, so expedited handling matters. Note: an automated reading of the PDF fact sheet gave different timeframes (48 h / 30 days); the press release wording is used here.
